# Cơm Gà 🇻🇳

::: {.dish-meta}
**Region:** Vietnam (Hội An & Tam Kỳ), with cousins across mainland SE Asia  ·  **Family:** Poach & serve (turmeric rice)
**Serves:** 4  ·  **Active time:** 50 minutes  ·  **Total:** 1 hour 20 min
**Assembly:** 🍚 Chicken over rice — herb-tossed shredded chicken piled on stock-cooked rice
:::

Golden turmeric rice cooked in chicken stock, crowned with poached chicken torn
and tossed with onion, chili, and a fistful of Vietnamese herbs. *Cơm gà* is the
central-Vietnamese answer to the whole region's love of chicken and rice — lighter,
herbier, and brighter than its ancestors.

## The story

*Cơm gà* means simply "chicken rice," and it belongs to the same great
[Hainanese-diaspora family](hainanese-chicken-rice.qmd) that spread across
Southeast Asia with Chinese traders and migrants. But the version that made it
famous — **Cơm Gà Hội An**, from the old trading port on Vietnam's central coast
(and its rival in nearby Tam Kỳ) — is unmistakably Vietnamese.

Where Hainanese chicken rice is cool and restrained, cơm gà is a salad as much as a
plate of rice: the poached chicken is shredded and tossed with thinly sliced onion,
sharp **rau răm** (Vietnamese coriander), lime, and fish sauce, then heaped over
rice that's been simmered in the poaching stock and tinted gold with turmeric. It
arrives with pickled vegetables, fresh chili, and a small bowl of the broth to sip.

## Ingredients

**Chicken & stock**

- 1 whole chicken, about 1.5 kg (3.3 lb)
- 5 cm ginger, smashed; 3 shallots, halved; 3 scallions
- 2 tsp salt

**Turmeric rice**

- 300 g (1.5 cups) jasmine rice, rinsed until nearly clear
- 2 tbsp rendered chicken fat or neutral oil
- 2 shallots, minced; 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp ground turmeric (or 1 tbsp grated fresh)
- 450 ml (scant 2 cups) reserved chicken stock
- Salt

**Chicken salad topping**

- ½ onion, sliced paper-thin and soaked in cold water 10 min
- Large handful **rau răm** (Vietnamese coriander), plus mint and cilantro
- 1 tbsp gluten-free fish sauce, 1 tbsp lime juice, 1 tsp sugar
- 1 red chili, sliced; crispy fried shallots to finish

**Nước chấm (dipping sauce)**

- 2 tbsp gluten-free fish sauce, 2 tbsp lime juice, 1 tbsp sugar
- 4 tbsp warm water, 1 clove garlic minced, 1 chili minced

**To serve:** *đồ chua* (pickled carrot & green papaya), cucumber, extra herbs,
and a bowl of the warm broth

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Gluten-free · dairy-free:** naturally both — rice, chicken, and herbs. The only
thing to check is the **fish sauce** (choose a gluten-free brand) and that your
crispy fried shallots weren't dusted in wheat flour.
:::

## Method

### Poach the chicken

1. Rub the chicken with the salt. Bring a pot of water (enough to submerge it) to a
   gentle boil with the ginger, shallots, and scallions. Lower the chicken in
   breast-side down.
2. Return to the barest simmer, cover, and **turn off the heat**. Rest, covered,
   45–50 minutes, until the thigh reads 68–70 °C (155–160 °F). Lift out into an ice
   bath for 5 minutes to firm the meat. **Reserve the stock.**
3. When cool, tear the meat off the bone into shreds; discard skin or slice it thin
   to fold back in.

### Cook the turmeric rice

4. In a pot, warm the chicken fat and gently fry the shallots and garlic until
   fragrant, 1 minute. Stir in the turmeric and cook 30 seconds — it should smell
   earthy, not scorched.
5. Add the drained rice and toast 2 minutes until the grains glisten gold. Pour in
   450 ml reserved stock and a good pinch of salt. Boil, cover, drop to the lowest
   heat, cook 12–13 minutes, then rest 10 minutes off the heat. Fluff.

### Toss the chicken & assemble

6. Drain the onion. Toss the shredded chicken with the onion, torn herbs, fish
   sauce, lime, sugar, and chili — taste for a bright, salty-sour balance.
7. Whisk the nước chấm ingredients until the sugar dissolves.
8. Mound the golden rice into bowls, pile the chicken salad on top, and shower with
   fried shallots and more herbs. Serve with *đồ chua*, cucumber, sliced chili, a
   bowl of broth to sip, and the nước chấm to spoon over.

## Across the mainland

Cơm gà is one node in a web of related chicken-rice dishes across Southeast Asia —
all descendants of the same poached-chicken-and-stock-cooked-rice idea:

- **Thailand — *Khao Man Gai*:** the closest to the Hainanese original; poached
  chicken over rice cooked in stock, served with a punchy fermented-soybean-and-
  ginger chili sauce.
- **Cambodia — *Bai Moan*:** "chicken rice," often with the rice fried in garlic and
  chicken fat, chicken poached or roasted, and a dipping sauce of lime, pepper, and
  fish sauce.
- **Laos:** the *khao mun kai* idea travels here too, eaten with plenty of fresh
  herbs and a fiery *jeow* (chili dip) on the side.
- **Malaysia & Singapore:** the shared ancestor —
  [Hainanese Chicken Rice](hainanese-chicken-rice.qmd) — cool poached chicken with
  three sauces.

## Make it yours

- **Southern (Saigon) style — *cơm gà xối mỡ*:** skip the salad and serve a
  crisp-skinned fried or roasted chicken leg over the turmeric rice instead.
- Can't find *rau răm*? Lean on mint and cilantro; the dish loses a little of its
  peppery edge but stays delicious.
- Make it a full spread with extra *đồ chua* and a plate of herbs so everyone builds
  their own bowl.
